newsitem.title: USA: Three U.S. drug firms post strong Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: Three U.S. drug firms post strong Q3 results.

text.p: Johnson and Johnson, Merck and Co. Inc. and Schering-Plough Corp. Wednesday beat Wall Street expectations with their third-quarter earnings, using higher-margin new products to fight off the impact of a strong U.S. dollar.
The firm dollar, which trimmed about two percentage points off each company's sales by lowering foreign revenue in dollar terms, was offset by higher sales volume and cost cutting, analysts said.

Whitehouse Station, N.J.-based Merck posted net income of $1.0 billion, or 83 cents a share, up from $861.9 million a year ago. It was the first time Merck, the largest U.S. pharmaceutical company, posted a billion dollars in quarterly profits.
The earnings per share were up from 70 cents a year ago and beat the consensus Wall Street estimate of 81 cents.
"The company's hitting on all cylinders, and the new products are doing very well," NatWest Securities analyst Jack Lamberton said.
Merck's biggest seller was the cholesterol-lowering drug Zocor, which had third-quarter sales of $725 million, a 41 percent gain over 1995's third quarter.
Other new drugs, including the Cozaar and Hyzaar high blood pressure treatments and Fosamax for osteoporosis, also posted strong sales gains in the quarter, Merck said.
Newly launched drugs typically carry higher prices and heftier profit margins than older medications.
Shares in Merck ended up 75 cents at $72 in New York Stock Exchange trading.

New Brunswick, N.J.-based Johnson and Johnson posted third-quarter net income of $750 million, or 56 cents a share, up from $623 million, or 48 cents a share, a year ago. It beat industry analysts' consensus estimate of 55 cents a share.

Its earnings were partly fuelled by strong growth in the company's consumer product lines, which were up 8.4 percent in the quarter over the year-ago period, led by the Tylenol and Neutrogena brands, analysts said.
It also got a boost from products from its recently acquired Cordis Corp. and UltraCision Inc. surgical products divisions, they said.
"It was a very solid quarter and new product launches continue to drive growth," said Salomon Brothers analyst Eli Kammerman.
Johnson and Johnson ended up 25 cents at $51.25 on the NYSE.

Madison, N.J.-based Schering-Plough reported third-quarter net income of $291.7 million, or 79 cents a share, up from $252.6 million, or 68 cents a share, a year ago and above the consensus forecast of 78 cents per share.

Third-quarter worldwide sales of its non-sedating antihistimine Claritin line totalled $323 million, up 73 percent, while sales of the anti-cancer/anti-viral agent Intron A were $138 million, up 21 percent, the company said.
The sales of the drugs worked to offset declines in the Proventil inhaler asthma treatment, and for Eulexin, a prostate cancer drug, due to U.S. competition.

Some industry analysts have said Schering-Plough could have a tougher time in 1997 as Claritin faces growing compeitition from other allergy drugs, including Hoechst AG's Allegra and Pfizer Inc.'s Zyrtec.
Schering-Plough fell 75 cents to $64.25 on the NYSE.
